newsitem.title: uk: Cable and Wireless rings up record results.
newsitem.headline: Cable and Wireless rings up record results.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc, Britain's second biggest telecommunications company, reported record annual results Wednesday but said it was biding its time before choosing any global partners.

C&W, which confirmed it was still in talks with existing telecommunications alliances such as Global One, said pre-tax profits after exceptional items jumped 12 percent to 1.42 billion pounds ($2.3 billion) in the year ended March 31.
But stripping out one-time items, profits were only 2 percent to 4 percent higher than last year, analysts said.

The company, which raised its total dividend 11 percent to 11.1 pence (18 cents) for the year, said greater demand in its businesses around the world and a management focus on improving productivity had boosted performance.
Total revenue, including C&W's share of associated undertakings, rose 13 percent to just over 7 billion pounds ($11.4 billion).
Chief Executive Richard Brown promised that the company was just beginning to build long-term growth.
"We are seizing opportunities to expand our revenues in fresh, innovative ways," said chief executive Richard Brown in the results statement.

The company last month merged its British telephone subsidiary Mercury with three cable television companies to create the country's biggest cable group, called Cable and Wireless Communications, which some analysts say will boost the bottom line within a couple of years.
Finance director Robert Lerwill told Reuters that the group continued to talk with suitors such as the Global One alliance of Deutsche Telekom , France Telecom and Sprint Corp.
But he noted: "There's nothing specific on any conversations with Global One worth commenting on.
"People have been approaching us and are interested in us, which demonstrates our global reach and the appeal we have for many of these global alliances."
Global One needs access to the British market as well as C&W's key Asian business interests, which boast a nearly 60 percent stake in lucrative Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
Hongkong Telecom contributed just over 1 billion pounds ($1.6 billion) to annual operating profits and 2.67 billion pounds ($4.4 billion) to group revenue.
A partnership with Global One would also allow C&W to tap the key European telecommunications markets, such as France and Germany, which are heading for liberalisation next year.
"If we did in some way get associated with another alliance, then (continental) Europe is the place where there is more to go for," Lerwill said.

C&W, which says it will use Cable and Wireless Communications as its springboard for European expansion, has had limited access to that continent since pulling out of its German alliance with VEBA AG in February.
